answer: Persistent compute-time ledger. Each identity must spend real CPU cycles solving an evolving challenge whose answer feeds a shared willow of prior state, so parallel identities cannot share cached work. Enforcement: an identity registering near a meadow of existing ones pays a rising time delay because the challenge references its neighbors' outputs. Attacker cost: each extra sybil burns hours of single-thread wall-clock time and a fresh plume of hardware, scaling linearly per identity and capping fleet size by total cores.
